decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 4.25% to 4.5%. The vote was 12-0.

changes.quote: The unemployment rate has stabilized at a low level in recent months, and labor market conditions remain solid.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.
Reworded from the previous statement: “Inflation has made progress toward the Committee's 2 percent objective but remains somewhat elevated.”

changes.quote: Since earlier in the year, labor market conditions have generally eased, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In support of its goals, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.”

changes.quote: Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; Alberto G. Musalem; Jeffrey R. Schmid; and Christopher J. Waller.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Michael S. Barr; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle…”

changes.quote: Voting against the action was Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities.

The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments.
Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 21.76% APR costs about $90.67 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.55% and moved 0 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.04% would not change.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 135k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.9% over the past year (December 2024); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +2 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.47%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.05% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 92%, cut 8%, hike 0%.
